Ulverston Lantern Festival organisers look to 2027

28th September
By Matthew Holmes. Senior Reporter

Share

0 comments
0:00 / 0:00
Read More

Simpler Over Time
Ulverston Lantern Festival returned on September 19 (Image: Chris Warner)

0:00 / 1:59

The organisers of the Ulverston Lantern Festival have celebrated the success of its return with donations needed to make 2027 just as special.

The annual event lit up the streets of the south Cumbrian market town on Saturday, September 19.

The date has already been set for its return on September 18, 2027 with people encouraged to share their ideas for themes at the Ulverston Lantern Festival Facebook page.

The committee behind the event said: "You were fantastic as were the bands bringing the uplifting beats to the thousands who came to see: BLAST Furness, Boom Dang, BJamba, the Staveley Kookaburra All Stars, and Drum Nation.

"Huge thanks as ever too to all our volunteer traffic marshals and stewards who kept the whole do safely parading on."

More than 7,000 people and 1,400 lanterns made their way from County Square to Ford Park to create a River of Light as part of the occasion earlier this month.

The ‘Dusk till Dawn’ theme inspired creations such as giant owls, bats, foxes, fairy tale coaches, UFOs, moons, and stars.

Donations for next year's festival to ensure its long-term future can be given here.

"Thank you too to those who generously loaded our collection buckets on the night and online," the committee added.

"As a volunteer-run event we rely on donations and lantern kit sales to cover most of our costs and keep going, so if you haven't already, chip in and we shall invest it in more sticks, glue and all the rest for more spectacular creations next year.

"If you’d like to join us to shape next year's event please message the page with your email and we’ll be sure to put an invite to the AGM in your inbox."

Crews from St John's Ambulance helped marshal the event this year, with the festival backed by the likes of CGP Books, Wax Lyrical, Ulverston Town Council, the Town Land Trust, Westmorland and Furness Council, and Travis Perkins.
